PullRequest.Title: accounts: let the default account be a remembered Microsoft account
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Stacked on #348960, which adds `asGitHubAccount`. Read that one first.

## What this changes

Behind `chat.agentHost.copilot.m365.enabled` (off by default), the default account service can produce a Microsoft account as the default account.

**There is no user-visible change.** Nothing in production remembers a Microsoft account yet; a later change makes Copilot setup do that. The one way to reach the new path today is to write the account preference described below by hand with the setting on.

**Nothing changes for GitHub accounts or for a window without an account**, with the setting on or off. With the setting off no new code path runs. With it on and no remembered account, the only addition is reading one stored preference; no Microsoft session is read and no extra default account update happens. Tests count the authentication lookups for both cases, and the policy tests below compare against a window without an account.

The Microsoft account path was not run in the product, because nothing can reach it yet. The GitHub path was checked in a local build with the setting off and on; see Validation.

- `asGitHubAccount` returns `undefined` for an account of the Microsoft authentication provider. Every reader that #348960 moved therefore treats a Microsoft default account like no account, and makes no GitHub request for it.
- `IDefaultAccountService` and `IDefaultAccountProvider` get `rememberMicrosoftAccount` and `forgetMicrosoftAccount`. Both resolve once this window's default account has been updated.
- `DefaultAccountProvider` looks for a remembered Microsoft account ahead of the GitHub path. If that account has a session, it is the default account. No GitHub request is made for it and it has no entitlement data.
- `ChatEntitlementRequests.getSessions` no longer falls back to every GitHub session in the window when the default account is not a GitHub account.

## How the choice is stored

With the existing account preference of `IAuthenticationExtensionsService`, under the key `vscode.copilot-default-account` for the Microsoft provider. That key is not an extension id, so the Manage Extension Account Preferences picker does not list it.

The preference is used as it is, with its existing behavior: it stores the account's label, the workspace copy is read before the application copy, and its change event fires only in the window that wrote it. Another window reads the choice when it next updates its default account.

## What a Microsoft default account does

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Setting off | Nothing new runs. No Microsoft session is read. |
| Setting on, no remembered account | As before. Microsoft session changes, provider registration and other extensions' Microsoft account preferences cause no default account update. |
| Remembered account has a session | It is the default account. |
| Remembered account has no session | The GitHub path runs as before. The preference is kept. |
| Microsoft provider neither declared nor registered | The Microsoft sessions are not read. The GitHub path runs. |
| Reading the Microsoft sessions fails | The window keeps the account it has, whether GitHub, Microsoft or none. At startup that is no account until the provider registers. |
| The account's session is removed and none remains | The account is forgotten and the default account is updated. |

Keeping the account on a failed lookup is deliberate. A failed lookup is neither a sign-in nor a sign-out, which is how the GitHub path already treats its own failed lookup. Falling back to a GitHub account instead would make a window that chose Microsoft briefly use GitHub on a slow start. The cost: if the Microsoft provider never becomes usable, that window stays without an account until the choice is cleared.

`signIn()` does not forget a remembered Microsoft account.

## Policy

A Microsoft default account does not change policy state. It gets what a window without an account gets.

- In `setDefaultAccount`, policy data, the managed settings compatibility error and the Copilot token info change only when a GitHub account is gained, replaced or lost. For GitHub accounts and for no account this is what the code did before: the no-account branch could not run from "no account" because of the early return for an unchanged account.
- The rule of the no-account branch moves into `applyPolicyWithoutAccount`, unchanged, so that replacing a GitHub account by a Microsoft account applies it too.
- In `fetchDefaultAccount`, every return that is not a GitHub account blocks managed settings freshness without a token, as the existing no-account returns do.
- `resolveGitHubUrl` uses the configured provider for a Microsoft account, as it does without an account.

No production file under `src/vs/workbench/services/policies` changes. One difference remains there and is not addressed here: when approved account organizations are configured, `AccountPolicyService` reports a Microsoft account as the wrong provider, and no account as no account. Both are restricted.

## Not in this change

- Remembering the account in Copilot setup, forgetting it when setup fails or the user signs out, and what the Agent Host is sent. A later change.
- Any change to what the title bar, account menus or chat views show. They show a Microsoft default account as signed in because they only ask whether there is an account; that is not reachable until something remembers one.
- The entitlement state. With a Microsoft account it is the existing `Unresolved`.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the 21 changed files: passed.
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`, then `scripts\test.bat --run <file>` for the 14 changed test files together: 1079 passing, 2 failing. The two failures are `NewChatWidget` tests ("Work in Parallel, as its first request is sent in its folder") that fail the same way on this Windows machine on unmodified `main`.
- No existing test's assertions were edited. Three test doubles in `copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts` got an `authenticationProvider`; see below. The only removed lines in test files are import lines.

What CI found on the first push. Three tests of the Copilot chat sessions provider failed. Their doubles handed out a default account that had entitlement data only, and `CloudAutomationStore`, which that provider constructs, now reads the account's authentication provider through `asGitHubAccount`. The account service cannot produce such an account: the account is built in two places, both in `DefaultAccountProvider`, and both set the provider. So the doubles were completed and the accessor was left strict. I had run the changed test files only; the failing file was not among them.

Six more doubles of the same entitlement-only shape exist, in `editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts`, `cloudSandboxDraftPreparationService.test.ts` and `cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts`. They are unchanged, because the code they exercise does not read the account through the accessor. They would fail the same way if it came to.

After that fix, on this head: `pnpm run typecheck-client` passed. A wider selection of 205 test files (the changed ones, every test file that imports one of the nine reader modules, and every test file that imports a file that imports one) gave 16428 passing, 32 failing. The 32 are 2 `NewChatWidget`, 28 `ChatListRenderer` and 2 `Sessions - SessionsList` tests; the same tests, by title, fail on this Windows machine on unmodified `main`. The browser unit tests were not run locally.

`main` was merged into the base branch and then into this one at a commit from November 19 that is not the latest, because the local environment could not install the dependencies of a later `main`.

What the new tests show:

- Policy: the same sequence runs in a window without an account and in a window with a Microsoft default account, and the policy data, compatibility error, Copilot token info and freshness are asserted equal to each other and to a literal. Sequences: startup with and without a refresh requirement, startup with cached policy, a refresh requirement that appears while the account is unchanged, a GitHub account replaced by a Microsoft account compared with that account signing out, forgetting with cached policy, and a failed lookup. Two of these failed before the fix they cover, on an earlier state of this branch.
- The rule extracted into `applyPolicyWithoutAccount` has a test that passes on the code before the extraction and after it.
- Each reader that #348960 moved has a test with a Microsoft default account. With `asGitHubAccount` temporarily put back to returning its argument, the accessor test and six reader tests fail. Four tests pass either way, because the code they cover already rejected an account of another provider; they are marked as pinning existing behavior.
- As a local experiment that is not part of this change, I repeated the field rename described in #348960. Production errors went from 48 to 52. The four extra are in `DefaultAccountProvider` itself, where it builds and compares the Microsoft account; the other 14 files are unchanged.

Live check of the GitHub path, on a local build of the first commit of this branch, before `main` was merged in again (the merge changed no dependency), signing in with a GitHub.com account. It was run twice, each time with a new empty profile: once with default settings and once with `chat.agentHost.copilot.m365.enabled` on.

- Before sign-in the Agents window showed the signed-out notice and the title bar offered sign-in.
- After sign-in the title bar and the account panel showed the GitHub account with its plan, the Agent Host log showed the authentication calls for the GitHub API, and models were listed.
- One chat message completed.
- An editor window opened from the Agents window listed the GitHub account in its Accounts menu, and its log showed the default account available and the entitlement resolved.
- After closing and starting again on the same profile, the window was signed in without a prompt.
- Sign Out returned the window to the signed-out notice and the Agent Host cleared its GitHub token.
- With the setting on, the default account in the window's log was the GitHub account throughout, and the Agent Host log showed authentication calls for the GitHub API only.

Both runs behaved the same, with two observations. Neither is in code this change touches. With the setting on, the sign-in dialog at first start stays open where it is otherwise dismissed; an earlier run of the commit below this one in the stack did the same. In the editor window the Copilot status bar entry read "Sign In" although the account and entitlement were resolved. By reading the code, that entry shows its setup form while Copilot setup is not completed in the profile, whatever the account. This was not compared with a build without this change.

Not checked: a Microsoft default account in the product, a GitHub Enterprise account, and the policy behavior with managed settings present. The behavior in a second window is tested with a fake of the authentication service's preference event.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub or signed-out window startup and refresh, with the Microsoft setting disabled or enabled without a remembered account
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DefaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount waits for provider initialization. Initialization waits for authentication-provider availability, managed-settings initialization, GitHub session discovery, and any required entitlement/policy requests. Classic web without remote skips provider initialization as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await native and file managed-settings snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold clients issue one native snapshot call and two file snapshot calls. Successful warm initialization reuses promises and adds no snapshot calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization preceded GitHub discovery before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Account discovery waits for initialization of these sources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the bounded managed-settings file and maintain its watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial file read, then debounced reads on file changes; not one read per account refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same watcher, file-size limit, initialization barrier, and debounce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial file snapshot is awaited; later refreshes use initialized state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover GitHub accounts and retrieve sessions through the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two session RPCs per successful discovery attempt: getAccounts internally calls getSessions, followed by the selected-account getSessions. Up to three attempts on failure. No Microsoft RPC without a preference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical GitHub discovery and retry count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session discovery must complete before default-account resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch GitHub entitlements, token entitlements, managed settings, and optionally MCP registry metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one successful request per required uncached endpoint, up to four endpoints. Failed authentication can try additional eligible sessions; rate-limit backoff can suppress requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same endpoint selection, cache conditions, eligible-session retry loop, and ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Entitlements precede the parallel token/managed-settings requests; optional MCP lookup follows token resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One default-account provider per window; authentication sessions for the configured GitHub provider; refreshes from focus, the hourly poll, configuration, and followed authentication events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing 100 ms ThrottledDelayer debounces updates and its Throttler permits one active reconciliation with one coalesced pending task per window. GitHub discovery is sequential; token and managed-settings requests can run concurrently after entitlements.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The Microsoft preference is read from existing in-memory workspace/application storage only when enabled. No preference means no Microsoft sessions are read. GitHub policy/entitlement data keeps its account/server scoping and one-hour freshness; successful managed-settings initialization is reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the added gates, initialization barrier, discovery helper, RPC bridge, throttler, and cache checks; added tests also count absence of Microsoft lookups and unrelated-event updates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual startup and request durations are not measured. Session counts, policy-file sizes, and authentication failures vary by installation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: common GitHub and signed-out paths retain their previous expensive-boundary counts; the enabled/no-preference path adds only bounded local preference/availability checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore or refresh a remembered Microsoft default account, including stale preferences and failed lookups
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the unchanged managed-settings initialization, fetchDefaultAccount awaits one Microsoft session-list read. A matching account finishes without GitHub discovery or entitlement requests. An empty successful lookup falls through to GitHub; a failed lookup keeps the current account.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Microsoft account-shaped sessions from the authentication extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per executed reconciliation when enabled, a preference exists, and the Microsoft provider is available. The provider enumerates cached account entries and returns one session per distinct homeAccountId, not one RPC or token request per account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Default-account reconciliation did not read Microsoft sessions; it performed GitHub discovery instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This read is awaited before selecting Microsoft or falling through to GitHub.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: If not registered, activate Microsoft authentication and initialize its existing secret-backed public-client cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold activation loads the existing client-id list and initializes cached clients once per extension activation. Warm all-sessions reads only enumerate in-memory PCAs/accounts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Microsoft activation/cache loading was not initiated by default-account discovery, though other existing features could already activate it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold provider activation is awaited; registered-provider warm reads do not repeat cache initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing one-time legacy token migration during cold authentication activation, if migration has not completed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only legacy unmigrated installations; refresh tokens grouped by client/tenant and migrated within those groups. Normal warm undefined-scope session enumeration performs no token acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The migration implementation already existed but was not activated from Microsoft default-account discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Conditional migration completes before provider registration; absent after migration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run existing GitHub session discovery only after a successful Microsoft lookup with no matching session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The stale-preference case adds one Microsoft RPC before the unchanged two GitHub RPCs per successful discovery attempt. Matching Microsoft accounts and Microsoft lookup failures make no GitHub discovery call from this reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GitHub discovery ran directly without the Microsoft check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fallback discovery is sequential after the Microsoft read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cached public-client applications and their account entries, deduplicated by homeAccountId into one returned session per Microsoft account; one remembered label per window; focus/hourly/explicit reconciliations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One throttled reconciliation per window; authentication extension operations serialize per provider through SequencerByKey. Cold PCA initialization uses Promise.allSettled across cached clients, while the warm enumeration itself is synchronous in the extension host.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Microsoft account enumeration uses the provider's existing in-memory account cache and does not mint tokens. The preference is retained on empty results or errors so later session/provider events can reconcile it. Existing successful source-initialization caches remain effective. A stable account is deep-equality suppressed before notifications.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected actual Microsoft undefined-scopes branch, cached account getter, homeAccountId deduplication, RPC serialization, activation path, and feature/preference guards. Repository search found no production consumer that remembers an account beyond the service wrappers themselves.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Microsoft selection currently requires externally populated preference state; product prevalence and cold authentication-cache duration are unknown. Legacy migration prevalence is also unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added boundary is a single guarded authoritative account lookup required for the new selection, not per-account token/network fan-out. Cold activation uses existing provider initialization; no unnecessary repeated heavy initialization was established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remember, forget, or sign out a Microsoft account; react to Microsoft session/provider/preference changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Remember/forget promises wait for the window's throttled account reconciliation. Removal of the current Microsoft session first reads remaining sessions; if the account has disappeared, it clears the preference and reconciles the fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update or remove the remembered account label in existing workspace and application storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two storage mutations per remember or forget, using one fixed preference key per scope; persistence uses the existing storage lifecycle rather than an awaited per-account transaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Microsoft-default-account preference was written or removed by this service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local mutation precedes reconciliation; the returned promise waits for reconciliation, not a new explicit disk flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read remaining Microsoft accounts after removal of the selected session, then reconcile the default account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Ordinary followed changes cause one Microsoft list RPC per coalesced reconciliation. Selected-session removal adds one direct list RPC; if the account remains, reconciliation adds one more. If absent, forgetting avoids a second Microsoft RPC and may perform existing GitHub fallback discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Microsoft session changes were ignored by the default-account provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The remaining-account read precedes forgetting/reconciliation; unrelated Microsoft events without remembered/current state return without discovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One remembered preference; actual account-list change events from the Microsoft provider. Events are account changes, not every token refresh. Bulk changes are buffered/deduplicated by the provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconciliation remains debounced and serialized per window. Removal checks occur outside that throttler, but extension-host Microsoft operations serialize per provider. Provider account events are already buffered and deduplicated; no per-token-refresh feedback loop was found.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Preference reads are local; remember's synchronous preference event and explicit update normally coalesce through the existing delayer. No growing map or session history is added. Microsoft sessions remain backed by cached account metadata; equal resolved accounts suppress account notifications.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced real preference-event emission, absence of removal-event emission, direct and throttled lookups, provider account-change semantics, and disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of genuine account changes and bursts from multiple clients is unmeasured; expected returned data is a user's account list, not session/token history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance bug: the extra removal lookup is bounded verification of account disappearance, normal events coalesce, unrelated events are gated, and no new unbounded retention or heavyweight recreation is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Policy initialization and GitHub-to-Microsoft or Microsoft-to-no-account transitions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial policy settlement waits for default-account initialization. State transitions update policy/freshness and notify existing policy consumers; Microsoft resolution does not fetch GitHub policy data.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update native managed-settings definitions when existing policy subscribers reevaluate policies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one native definition-update call per policy reevaluation when managed-setting definitions exist. Native service reuses its watcher when definitions are equal; it does not recreate a watcher per unchanged account poll.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscribers and native-definition updates handled GitHub account changes and sign-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Policy reevaluation awaits the native definition result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist or clear the existing cached GitHub policy record on actual policy changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing cached record; equality suppresses identical writes. Microsoft-to-Microsoft and Microsoft-to-no-account transitions do not newly serialize Microsoft policy state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extracted no-account policy rule already handled loss of a GitHub account with the same retained-policy condition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local storage mutation accompanies policy notification; no new awaited persistence boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured policy definitions and managed-setting keys; actual default-account/freshness transitions, rather than every session enumeration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing default-account throttling controls discovery. Policy event handlers can overlap asynchronous reevaluations as before; unchanged native definitions reuse initialization and watcher state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached policy state remains scoped to the GitHub account/server and preserves the existing blocking-refresh retention rule. Source snapshots are reused; failed Microsoft lookup keeps existing account/policy state. Equal accounts and equal policy values suppress notifications.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: compared extraction against deleted lines and inspected policy subscribers, conditional native definition updates, equality checks, and native watcher reuse.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Policy-definition count and native watcher latency vary; no measurements. No added collection-wide hot-loop mechanism was identified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the changed policy branches preserve the prior loss-of-GitHub rule and do not add new policy fetches, caches, or repeated watcher creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub-dependent welcome profiles, cloud automations, connectors/marketplace, client acquisition, and environment sharing with a Microsoft default account
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These features await initialized account state as needed and apply the changed asGitHubAccount guard. GitHub client acquisition and cloud automation operations reject/disable before GitHub API work; welcome-name loading and sharing enablement also stop before their GitHub lookups.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire authenticated GitHub clients and perform profile/automation API work only for eligible GitHub accounts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero profile or automation API requests for Microsoft default accounts. Existing GitHub sessions retain their prior profile-promise cache and client/catalogue lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GitHub API implementations and caches already existed. Before the PR the real default-account provider could not produce a Microsoft account; explicit provider checks already protected the welcome-profile path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Microsoft guards terminate these paths before remote work; profile fetches for GitHub remain background work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing connector authentication helper reads sessions for the configured GitHub provider before determining that no eligible default GitHub account is available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A directly reached helper can perform one existing GitHub session-list RPC even for a missing/filtered account; no connector network request follows without an eligible account. The new Microsoft account does not add an RPC per connector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helper already read GitHub sessions when the default account was absent. The diff changes account eligibility, not helper call multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The session read is awaited by that existing helper; normal marketplace query checks the unavailable account before querying.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For existing sharing, query agent-host environment identity and GitHub owner sessions when owner resolution is necessary; disable configured sharing on loss of its GitHub account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Microsoft sharing enablement rejects before session/host configuration work. Existing-registration withdrawal can use one environment-id call and one GitHub session read; an unknown Microsoft owner is not configured. A known previous GitHub owner can receive one disable operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Owner/provider checks and account-loss withdrawal already existed. The PR makes Microsoft accounts follow the unsupported-account branch rather than adding environment/workspace fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing withdrawal ordering awaits owner resolution/configuration; new sharing with Microsoft cannot start.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Feature requests and account transitions. For rejected Microsoft requests, effective repository/catalogue/profile request cardinality is zero, regardless of the user's repository or automation collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing cancellation, client lifetimes, per-store sequencers, and profile-promise coalescing remain in place. Rejected Microsoft paths do not launch per-repository or per-connector work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub client references and connector catalogue contexts are cleared/cancelled on actual eligible-account identity changes; cloud store reader-owned resources are disposed. Microsoft-to-Microsoft changes do not create GitHub stores. The marketplace's Microsoft session events no longer clear browse caches through the GitHub-session filter. Welcome-profile promises remain keyed by provider/session and coalesce requests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected accessor consumers, account guards, account-change resets, cloud store ownership/disposal, profile cache, and actual connector/withdrawal exceptions to early rejection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Feature enablement and existing sharing state vary. No performance timing or repository-scale benchmark was run.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-caused performance issue: the accessor chiefly removes eligible GitHub work for Microsoft accounts. Existing ancillary authentication/withdrawal calls do not become collection-scaling fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat entitlement resolution and Copilot Free signup with a Microsoft default account
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Entitlement resolution waits for initialized account state and returns Unresolved from missing entitlement data without a network request. signUpFree awaits getSessions, receives an empty list for Microsoft, and returns before signup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read configured GitHub authentication sessions for eligible signup paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero session-list RPCs for a Microsoft default account. GitHub selected-session lookup uses one RPC, with a second fallback lookup only if the selected session is absent; no-account uses one RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The helper fell back to configured GitHub sessions after an accessor miss; the new explicit non-GitHub-account branch suppresses that fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Signup waits for these existing authentication reads, but the Microsoft branch now terminates immediately after account initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST Copilot Free signup using eligible GitHub sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero requests for Microsoft accounts. Existing eligible paths normally stop after one successful session request, with additional session attempts or user-confirmed retry only on existing failure paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing fallback could supply configured GitHub sessions; the PR prevents that for a non-GitHub default account rather than adding requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A signup POST is awaited only when eligible sessions exist.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One signup action and the configured GitHub session list; eligible session count matters only for unchanged GitHub/no-account signup paths.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new parallel requests. Existing signup session attempts are sequential; Microsoft executes none.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getDefaultAccount reads initialized state, not a fresh account discovery for each caller. Entitlement resolution consumes account metadata and does not retry missing Microsoft entitlement data over the network. Existing cancellation replaces pending entitlement resolutions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced getSessions caller, explicit early return, signup guard, and metadata-only entitlement resolution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Signup frequency and failed eligible-session counts are unmeasured. Microsoft reachability is currently gated by remembered state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression and no confirmed historical performance-regression fix: the changed branch suppresses GitHub work for newly supported Microsoft state that the pre-diff production provider could not create.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base a46ab5288363fed07e521b7958ec7cbf834d65ac. Inspected the complete 22-file inventory and every diff page, including all three bounded pages of the large account-test patch. Traced account initialization, authentication RPC/provider behavior, cache/coalescing, policy I/O, and downstream GitHub guards. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or blame-eligible historical regression fix was established. Static review only; measured timings and live Microsoft-account behavior are unavailable. The focus guide was requested, but the tool exposed only a preview of its oversized response; the full loaded skill instructions and learned-regression document supplied the mechanism/evidence criteria.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
